title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Scammers are using generative AI and deepfake technology to impersonate real people, including a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants seeking legal services. The scams combine voice cloning, fake photographs, spoofed phone numbers, and personal information harvested from social media to make fraudulent solicitations appear legitimate. This is an impersonation failure: AI systems were deployed by criminals to deceive people into believing they were communicating with trusted professionals or family members.

The deployment happened on social media and through phone calls, where victims encountered deepfaked voices and fabricated personas before they could verify the identity through independent means. No safeguard was in place before victims engaged with scammers, as the victims themselves bore the burden of authentication. Catching this would have required either robust caller verification systems on phone networks, platform controls to detect and remove deepfaked audio and video, or public awareness sufficient for targets to independently confirm identity before engaging.

It is not established whether any particular AI system or platform knowingly enabled these scams, whether the voice-cloning or image-generation tools were built for this purpose, or what specific consequences resulted from these frauds beyond the financial losses reported.

summary:
# Summary

Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence and deepfake technology to commit fraud across Georgia and South Florida. The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report found that Americans reported nearly 893 million dollars in losses from AI-enabled scams last year. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately 800,000 dollars in a cryptocurrency scam. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints totaling nearly 40 million dollars in losses, while Georgia had 71 complaints resulting in over 10 million dollars in losses.

Criminals are using generative AI to clone voices from social media, create fake photographs, spoof phone numbers, and research personal relationships to make scams more convincing. Common schemes include romance scams, fake investment opportunities, emergency calls from supposed grandchildren, and distress scams. Financial institutions warn customers that these impersonation attempts are becoming harder to detect. Authorities recommend establishing secret code words with family members to verify identity, verifying urgent requests through known phone numbers, and reporting suspected scams to law enforcement rather than responding immediately to suspicious communications.
